As staff have worked with numerous community partners to explore interim emergency solutions
for daytime space and food security, it's become clear that no one organization has
the ability to fill the immediate gaps for our community.
Capacity in our community is limited and highly relying on volunteers and partnerships with
community organizations and their expertise who support those in need.
In an effort to provide additional support to community nonprofit organizations, the
city will be launching a one-time emergency community grant for daytime space and food
security program.
We will have up to $120,000 available for community organizations who believe they are
in a position to increase the availability of daytime space or meals in the community
between now and March 1st.
Our aim is to launch this program later this week, and I'd encourage any organizations
who are interested to follow our social channels for more information or be in touch with myself
or Kushla Matthews, our Manager of Community and Affordable Housing, and we'd be happy
to share more details about the grant opportunity.
